claim: A peer-reviewed 2025 study found residual manufacturing DNA in COVID-19 mRNA vaccines far above regulatory limits, and an undeclared genetic-control sequence in the Pfizer product. Plasmid DNA — the circular bacterial DNA used as the template to mass-produce the vaccine's mRNA — is expected only as a trace residue after manufacturing, and the U.S. FDA and World Health Organization (WHO) cap it at 10 nanograms (ng) per dose. Measuring 32 vials across 16 lots from Ontario, Canada, Speicher, Rose and McKernan reported in the journal Autoimmunity (2025) total DNA of 371–1,548 ng/dose in Pfizer and 1,130–6,280 ng/dose in Moderna vials by fluorometry (tens to hundreds of times the limit), while the FDA's preferred method (qPCR, which counts only amplifiable fragments) put some vials within limit and others over — so the correct yardstick is itself disputed. They detected the SV40 (Simian Virus 40) promoter-enhancer, a DNA sequence that drives strong gene expression, only in the Pfizer vials; it was not identified in the sequences Pfizer originally filed with regulators. Health Canada's own account is more precise: 'although the full DNA sequence of the Pfizer plasmid was provided at the time of initial filing, the sponsor did not specifically identify the SV40 sequence,' and the agency said it 'expects sponsors to identify any biologically functional DNA sequences within a plasmid (such as an SV40 enhancer) at the time of submission' — so the sequence was in the filing, unflagged, rather than absent from it. Responding to Florida's surgeon general in December 2023, the FDA did not deny the sequence is present — it stated that 'No SV40 proteins are encoded for or are present in the vaccines,' that animal studies showed 'no evidence for genotoxicity,' and that across 'over a billion doses… no safety concerns related to residual DNA have been identified.' What is established is that the residual DNA and the SV40 promoter sequence are present and were not disclosed on the filed sequences; contested is the correct measurement method and whether there is any health effect. Genomics professor Phillip Buckhaults told the South Carolina Senate (September 2023) each shot carries 'about 200 billion pieces of plasmid DNA' that 'can and likely will integrate' into cells, while adding he believed this was 'a scientific and regulatory oversight, not a nefarious intent.' No study has demonstrated such integration in a vaccinated person.

sources.label: Speicher, Rose, McKernan et al., 'Quantification of residual plasmid DNA and SV40 promoter-enhancer sequences in Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna modRNA COVID-19 vaccines from Ontario, Canada' — Autoimmunity (2025), PMID 40913499

sources.quote: This means each shot has about 200 billion pieces of plasmid DNA encapsulated in the lipid nanoparticle. ... I believe this was a scientific and regulatory oversight, not a nefarious intent to transfect people and alter their DNA. But it needs to be fixed nonetheless.

notes: Built 2026-07-13 from the graphene-oxide dig (capture DabC5nzSptx). This is the substantive, PEER-REVIEWED 'undeclared contaminant' story that the graphene-oxide meme is a garbled version of — it is DNA, not graphene. Distinct from and adjacent to [[2021-graphene-oxide-vaccine-claim-001]] (the graphene claim, which has no indexed spectroscopic support). Tier discipline, all citations checked this session: (1) Speicher/Rose/McKernan, Autoimmunity 2025 = the peer-reviewed anchor, PMID 40913499 / DOI 10.1080/08916934.2025.2551517, ng/dose figures verbatim from the PubMed abstract; this is the peer-reviewed successor to the 2023 McKernan OSF preprint (b9t7m, preprint — labeled as such in the source list). DO NOT confuse with König & Kirchner, Methods Protoc (MDPI) 2024, which received an Expression of Concern — that EoC is NOT on the Autoimmunity paper. (2) Buckhaults SC Senate slides = official state-legislative record; note his 'can and likely will integrate' language is STRONGER than McKernan's own preprint, which explicitly presents no evidence of integration — so the claim brackets it with 'No study has demonstrated such integration in a vaccinated person.' His 'oversight, not nefarious intent' caveat is quoted so we don't pedestalize either side. (3) FDA Marks→Ladapo letter (fda.gov/media/174875/download, confirmed to resolve via browser UA; WebFetch is bot-blocked with 403/404 but the file is real) = the U.S. regulator on record; note the neutral nuance that Marks answers 'no SV40 proteins' while the finding is about the SV40 promoter/enhancer DNA sequence — Ladapo publicly flagged that as conflating two distinct things. Health Canada also confirmed the SV40 sequence is present/undeclared (written question Q-2665 44-1, answer in Hansard 335; the internal Dean Smith email says Pfizer 'chose not to' mention it) — not cited directly because the Hansard answer text wasn't fetched this pass; the FDA letter carries the regulator-acknowledgment weight. Established = presence + non-disclosure on filed sequences (peer-reviewed AND regulator-acknowledged). Contested = qPCR vs fluorometry yardstick; health significance; no demonstrated human genome integration in either direction. Per 'no official story as truth' + 'no fringe as truth': FDA's 'no concern' and Buckhaults' 'will integrate' are BOTH attributed, neither adopted. Not an EFTA-corpus subject (vaccine/DNA, no Epstein nexus). | 2026-08-01: tightened the non-disclosure sentence after pulling Health Canada's actual wording. The earlier phrasing ('not identified in the sequences Pfizer originally filed') could be read as the sequence being absent from the filing. Health Canada says the opposite and it matters: the full plasmid sequence WAS submitted, the SV40 element was simply not called out, and the agency says it expects sponsors to flag functional elements like an SV40 enhancer. That is a disclosure-practice failure, not a hidden ingredient — a narrower and better-supported claim. See [[2026-sv40-equivalence-claim-001]] for the plasmid map resolution and Health Canada's countervailing safety statement.
